narrativeReportMd:
# MessageHeader R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps the `MessageHeader` resource identity, but it introduces several local hard breaks. The highest-impact changes are the response correlation datatype/semantic change, mandatory endpoint wire-format changes, movement of `sender`, removal of several participant/routing fields, and R6-only widened reference/choice domains.

## Scope
This report compares the local R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition-MessageHeader.json` snapshots and differentials, plus directly bound local terminology for MessageHeader. Inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element/Extension changes are intentionally excluded from `findings[]`.

## Main migration themes
R4→R6 migration is not just a terminology update: several JSON paths change (`source.endpoint`/`destination.endpoint` to choice elements and root `sender` to `source.sender`), and some R4 fields have no local R6 replacement (`destination.target`, `enterer`, `author`, `responsible`). R6→R4 conversion also needs policy because R6 can omit endpoints, reference Endpoint resources, use canonical event definitions, and reference receiver/sender target types not allowed in R4.

## Highest-impact findings
The response identifier change (MessageHeader:TYPE_DOMAIN:MessageHeader.response.identifier:fe8312) is the most semantically significant because it changes both JSON shape and the identity being acknowledged. Endpoint choice conversions (MessageHeader:SERIALIZATION_OR_CODEGEN:MessageHeader.source.endpoint:32fe8b, MessageHeader:SERIALIZATION_OR_CODEGEN:MessageHeader.destination.endpoint:5b9d79) are broad wire-format breaks. The sender move (MessageHeader:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:MessageHeader.sender:620c70) is a path break with target-domain widening.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for response identifier policy, participant attribution removals, `destination.target` routing semantics, and any R6-to-R4 conversion of Endpoint references or new receiver/sender target types.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been less disruptive with deprecation periods, aliases, or new optional fields. The R6 designs are often cleaner and more expressive, but official cross-version mapping guidance would materially reduce migration risk.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze base Resource/DomainResource changes separately, and review Endpoint, EventDefinition, SubscriptionTopic, Provenance, and Task when designing concrete conversion rules.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 preserves the `MessageHeader` identity but contains local hard breaks. Top concerns are `response.identifier` changing from primitive id to Identifier/Bundle identity, endpoint and sender path changes, and removal of routing/provenance participant elements. The main uncertainty is the absence of official cross-version mapping rationale for the removed fields.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration requires both mechanical JSON rewrites and semantic policy. Mechanical rewrites include `source.endpoint`/`destination.endpoint` to choice properties and root `sender` to `source.sender`. Semantic decisions are needed for Bundle-vs-MessageHeader response correlation, removed participant roles, removed destination target routing, Endpoint references, canonical events, and widened receiver/sender target domains.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable local StructureDefinition deltas because both assigned StructureDefinitions are present and directly comparable. Confidence is lower for intended replacement semantics for removed participant/routing fields because no official diff, Jira rationale, or cross-version ConceptMap was available.

findings.title: MessageHeader.response.identifier changed from primitive id to complex Identifier and now identifies the original Bundle

oldState.summary: Required primitive id carrying the MessageHeader.id of the original message.

semanticText.definition: The MessageHeader.id of the message to which this message is a response.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a response identified the prior message by a primitive `id` string, serialized as `response.identifier`.

newState.summary: Required Identifier carrying the Bundle.identifier of the original message.

semanticText.definition: The Bundle.identifier of the message to which this message is a response.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the same element is a complex `Identifier` object and points at the enclosing message Bundle identifier rather than the MessageHeader resource id.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and serialization break for responses: an R4 `response.identifier` string is not valid where R6 requires an `Identifier` object, and an R6 Identifier object cannot be represented in R4 without collapsing or externalizing `system`, `value`, and other Identifier metadata. The semantic referent also changed from `MessageHeader.id` to `Bundle.identifier`, so a syntactic transform still needs identity-policy review.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Acknowledgement correlation is operationally important; an incorrect transform can cause responses to be associated with the wrong original message.

justification.inferredGoal: Align response correlation with the message Bundle identity rather than the MessageHeader resource id.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add a new Bundle-level Identifier element while retaining the R4 primitive response identifier for one transition release.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Correlating responses to the original message `Bundle.identifier` is a reasonable R6 goal, and a full `Identifier` is more robust than the R4 `MessageHeader.id` string. A less-breaking design exists, but it would not fully enforce the new correlation model and could permit conflicting acknowledgement identities, so the in-place break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `response.identifier` as the R4 primitive id for the original `MessageHeader`, add a new `response.bundleIdentifier` or similar `Identifier`, and define precedence or migration rules. That would preserve old JSON, but it creates parallel response-correlation mechanisms and leaves legacy messages semantically short of the R6 Bundle-identifier goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves old instances but leaves two correlation identifiers with safety and interoperability risk if they disagree.

evidence.detail: R4 has min 1..1, type `id`, short text "Id of original message".
evidence.quote: definition: The MessageHeader.id of the message to which this message is a response.

evidence.detail: R6 has min 1..1, type `Identifier`, short text "Bundle.identifier of original message".
evidence.quote: definition: The Bundle.identifier of the message to which this message is a response.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments are scoped to the changed child. A real migration must decide whether the R4 message id can safely become `Identifier.value` and what `Identifier.system` should be.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageHeader.response.identifier` is one of the clearest local hard breaks. R4 acknowledgements used a primitive id string for the original `MessageHeader.id`; R6 uses a full `Identifier` for the original message Bundle. Strict validators and generated models will reject the old JSON shape, and business logic that correlates acknowledgements by MessageHeader id must be revisited.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid response fragment such as `"identifier": "msg-123"` is not valid R6 because the element is now a complex datatype. Conversely, R6 can carry `Identifier.system`, `value`, `type`, `assigner`, and period data that R4 has no place to store in the primitive id. Even a syntactically successful migration can be semantically wrong if the source id was not the Bundle identifier.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, map the old string to `response.identifier.value` only after confirming that it is the identifier used for the original message Bundle; assign a stable `system` when one is known. For R6→R4, only a lossy projection to a single id string is possible unless an extension or side table preserves Identifier details. Test acknowledgement matching against historical messages before switching correlation logic.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 goal appears reasonable, but replacing the element in place was disruptive. A choice type or new optional element could have allowed old instances to validate while encouraging Bundle-level correlation. The tradeoff would have been a longer period of dual semantics.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed for each integration because the correct `Identifier.system` and the relationship between MessageHeader.id and Bundle.identifier are deployment-specific.

findings.title: MessageHeader.source.endpoint became optional endpoint[x] and added Endpoint references

semanticText.short: Actual message source address or id
semanticText.definition: Identifies the routing target to send acknowledgements to.

oldState.narrativeMd: Every valid R4 MessageHeader has a `source`, and every R4 `source` had to include the primitive URL-valued `endpoint` child.

newState.summary: Optional choice endpoint[x] with url or Reference(Endpoint).

semanticText.short: Actual source address or Endpoint resource
semanticText.definition: Identifies the routing target to send acknowledgements to.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 represents the same concept as a choice, serialized as `source.endpointUrl` or `source.endpointReference`, and no longer requires it.

facts.note: R6-to-R4 instances can now omit a value R4 required.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element keeps the same parent, requirements, and acknowledgement-routing definition, but converts the old URL child into a choice and adds an Endpoint reference option.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because `MessageHeader.source` is required in both releases and R4 required `source.endpoint`, every complete R4 MessageHeader contains a JSON property that R6 no longer defines. A mechanical R4→R6 transform can usually rename it to `source.endpointUrl`, but untransformed instances and generated R4 models fail. R6 also permits omission or `Reference(Endpoint)`, either of which is not directly valid in R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The source endpoint is used for acknowledgement routing and security decisions; incorrect or missing transforms can affect reply delivery.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow a richer Endpoint resource reference and make endpoint information optional when routing is handled elsewhere.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `source.endpoint` as the URL form and add an optional `source.endpointReference` for Endpoint resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting Endpoint references and allowing absent source endpoint information are reasonable goals, but replacing the required URL child with `endpoint[x]` forces every R4 source endpoint to be renamed. The same base R6 goal could have been met while preserving R4 instances by keeping the old URL child and adding a reference child, so this level of R4-to-R6 breakage was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A compatible design would keep `source.endpoint` as `0..1 url`, add `source.endpointReference` as `0..1 Reference(Endpoint)`, and add an invariant or conformance rule that at most one is populated. That supports Endpoint resources and optional routing while preserving old R4 messages. The cost is a less elegant non-choice shape and the risk that the legacy URL representation persists indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Less idiomatic than a FHIR choice and may leave a permanent legacy URL property, but an at-most-one rule can control ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 source.endpoint is min 1..1, type `url`.
R6 source.endpoint[x] is min 0..1, type `url` or `Reference(Endpoint)`.

examples.examplesMd: The old URL value maps cleanly to `endpointUrl`; `endpointReference` requires resolving or carrying the Endpoint resource when projecting back to R4.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageHeader.source.endpoint` changed from a required URL child to an optional choice. This is a wire-format and code-generation break even though the routing concept is recognizable: R4 JSON uses `endpoint`, while R6 URL content must use the choice property `endpointUrl`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Untransformed R4 instances with `source.endpoint` are old-valid/new-invalid under strict R6 validation because the element name changed. R6 instances with no source endpoint are valid in R6 but cannot satisfy R4 `source.endpoint` min=1. R6 `endpointReference` content also cannot be carried in the R4 primitive URL element without resolving it to an address or using an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, rename `source.endpoint` to `source.endpointUrl`. For R6→R4, require a policy: copy `endpointUrl` when present; for `endpointReference`, resolve the referenced Endpoint address if available or preserve the reference in an extension/side channel; reject or profile messages that omit the endpoint when an R4 representation is required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer Endpoint reference could have been introduced without renaming the existing primitive field, but FHIR choice typing provides a cleaner single logical endpoint element. The backwards-compatible alternative would avoid universal R4 instance rewrites but add another parallel field to the model.

findings.title: MessageHeader.destination.endpoint became optional endpoint[x] and added Endpoint references

oldState.summary: Required url in each destination backbone occurrence.

semanticText.definition: Indicates where the message should be routed to.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a `destination` repetition was not valid unless it contained a primitive URL-valued `endpoint` property.

newState.summary: Optional choice endpoint[x] with url or Reference(Endpoint).

semanticText.short: Actual destination address or Endpoint resource
semanticText.definition: Indicates where the message should be routed.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 serializes destination endpoint values as `endpointUrl` or `endpointReference`, and a destination can now omit the endpoint entirely.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element retains the destination routing definition and requirements while changing the element identity to a choice.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 destination that includes the required `endpoint` URL must be rewritten before R6 validation. In the reverse direction, R6 can now describe a destination without an endpoint or with an Endpoint reference, neither of which fits the R4 required primitive URL slot without additional resolution or policy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Destination endpoint information is central to message routing; failed transforms can affect delivery or acknowledgements.

justification.inferredGoal: Support Endpoint resources and allow destination routing to be conveyed by other means.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `destination.endpoint` as the URL form and add an optional `destination.endpointReference` for Endpoint resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of supporting Endpoint resources and optional destination routing is sound, but the choice conversion is not the only base-design path. Keeping the R4 URL element and adding a separate Endpoint reference would preserve existing destination-bearing messages while still enabling the new reference form, making the hard wire-format break probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep `destination.endpoint` as `0..1 url`, add `destination.endpointReference` as `0..1 Reference(Endpoint)`, and state that systems should use only one representation. The tradeoff is model clutter and possible long-lived duplicate endpoint representations, but those costs are moderate compared with invalidating every R4 destination URL property.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves existing routing URLs but keeps two endpoint representations that require mutual-exclusion and precedence guidance.

evidence.detail: R4 destination.endpoint is min 1..1, type `url`.
R6 destination.endpoint[x] is min 0..1, type `url` or `Reference(Endpoint)`.

examples.examplesMd: The omitted-endpoint R6 example is valid under the changed R6 cardinality but cannot be made R4-valid without supplying a URL endpoint.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageHeader.destination.endpoint` follows the same pattern as the source endpoint: the old required URL property was replaced by an optional choice. This is locally breaking for destination-bearing messages because old JSON uses the wrong property name for R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 destination containing `endpoint` is not valid R6 as-is; it must be transformed to `endpointUrl`. R6 destination entries can omit endpoint or use `endpointReference`, both of which create R6→R4 representability failures because R4 requires a primitive URL for each destination.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `destination[].endpoint` to R6 `destination[].endpointUrl`. When converting R6 to R4, require a destination URL, resolve referenced Endpoint resources where possible, or preserve unresolved Endpoint references outside the base R4 element. Include test cases for multiple destinations, omitted endpoints, and Endpoint references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This could have been less disruptive by keeping the old primitive element and adding a reference element. The R6 choice is internally consistent but imposes a mandatory wire-format rewrite and a reverse-conversion policy.

findings.title: Root MessageHeader.sender moved under source and added sender reference targets

oldState.summary: Optional root sender Reference to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization.

semanticText.short: Real world sender of the message
semanticText.definition: Identifies the sending system to allow the use of a trust relationship.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 placed the real-world sender directly under `MessageHeader.sender`.

newState.summary: Optional nested source.sender Reference to Device, Organization, Patient, Practitioner, or PractitionerRole.

semanticText.short: Real world sender of the message
semanticText.definition: Identifies the sending entity to allow the use of a trust relationship.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 nests the sender inside `source` and widens the allowed sender targets to include Device and Patient.

facts.newValue: Proposing to remove and rely on Task to convey this information.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short label, requirements, and trust-relationship use case match; R6 moved the element beneath the source backbone and updated its target profiles.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance with root `sender` is not valid against the R6 MessageHeader shape unless the element is moved to `source.sender`. Generated code and FHIRPath/search expressions also need path updates. In reverse, R6 `source.sender` can reference Device or Patient, which were not allowed R4 sender targets.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Sender identity can affect trust, authorization, audit, and routing decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Tie the real-world sender more directly to the message source component and broaden sender identity beyond practitioners and organizations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep root `MessageHeader.sender`, broaden its target types, and clarify that it represents the source-side sender.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Tying sender identity to the message source and allowing Device or Patient senders are reasonable goals. However, the R4 root `sender` already represented the real-world sender for trust/routing purposes, so R6 could have broadened that element and updated its definition or deprecation status without moving the path. The breaking move is therefore probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest compatible alternative is to retain `MessageHeader.sender` as `0..1 Reference` and add the new Device and Patient targets there, with text clarifying that it is the source-side sender and that future workflows may prefer Task or Provenance. If R6 also added `source.sender`, it would need at-most-one and precedence rules; simply living with the old path is the lower-risk compatibility option.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains a less tidy root-level placement and may delay convergence on `source.sender` or Task, but avoids a path break.

evidence.detail: R4 root sender exists as 0..1 Reference to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization.
R6 has nested source.sender as 0..1 Reference to Device, Organization, Patient, Practitioner, or PractitionerRole.
R6 comment notes a proposal to remove the element and rely on Task.
evidence.quote: Proposing to remove and rely on Task to convey this information.

examples.examplesMd: The R4→R6 path move is lossless for the original target types. R6 Patient or Device senders need an R4 extension or alternate representation.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageHeader.sender` did not disappear entirely, but its identity changed: it is now `MessageHeader.source.sender`. This breaks old instances and generated accessors while preserving much of the intended trust/routing semantics. R6 also permits sender references that R4 validators reject.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 content at the root `sender` path is old-valid/new-invalid until moved. R6 content at `source.sender` must be moved back for R4, and references to Patient or Device are not R4-valid sender targets. FHIRPath expressions, search logic, and generated model properties using the old root path need updates.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move root `sender` into `source.sender` during R4→R6 conversion. For R6→R4, move `source.sender` back only when the reference target is Organization, Practitioner, or PractitionerRole; otherwise use an extension, Task/Provenance context, or a project-specific policy. Review any security rules that used the sender path.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The path move is understandable, but not strictly backward-compatible. A deprecation period with both paths or a formal cross-version extension would have reduced migration pain. The R6 ballot comment suggesting future removal means implementers should avoid making new long-lived dependencies on this element without reviewing the messaging workflow.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact future role of `source.sender` is uncertain because the R6 comment mentions possible removal in favor of Task.

findings.title: MessageHeader.destination.target was removed with no exact local replacement

oldState.summary: Optional Reference(Device) identifying a particular delivery target within the destination.

semanticText.short: Particular delivery destination within the destination
semanticText.definition: Identifies the target end system in situations where the initial message transmission is to an intermediary system.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could specify a Device target for multi-hop routing inside each destination.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removed the local target child. Possible nearby elements such as `destination.endpoint[x]` and `destination.receiver` do not have identical semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances that used `destination.target` become invalid in R6 because the element is absent. The impact is narrower than the endpoint changes because the element was optional, but when used it carried routing information that may not be recoverable from other MessageHeader fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of a multi-hop target can route a message to the wrong application or require manual routing reconciliation.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify destination routing and possibly rely on Endpoint resources or receiver identity instead of a Device target child.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `destination.target` as deprecated while adding Endpoint-based routing and receiver guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Simplifying destination routing around Endpoint and receiver references is a plausible goal, but the local R6 model has no exact replacement for the R4 intermediary target device. Because `destination.target` was optional, retaining it as deprecated would have preserved old instances while allowing R6 guidance to prefer the newer routing model. The hard removal is probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A compatible base design would keep `destination.target` as `0..1 Reference(Device)`, mark it legacy or deprecated, and define how it relates to `destination.endpoint[x]`, `endpointReference`, and `receiver`. Profiles could discourage new use. The tradeoff is continued model clutter and possible routing ambiguity, but it avoids losing or rejecting explicit multi-hop target data.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains a legacy routing concept that can overlap with Endpoint or receiver and needs precedence guidance, but preserves multi-hop target data.

evidence.detail: R4 has destination.target as 0..1 Reference(Device).
evidence.quote: Identifies the target end system in situations where the initial message transmission is to an intermediary system.

evidence.detail: R6 MessageHeader has no element id `MessageHeader.destination.target`; the R6 differential includes destination.endpoint[x] and destination.receiver but not target.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative and not generally lossless: creating or selecting an Endpoint resource for a former Device target requires local routing knowledge.

findings.narrativeMd: `destination.target` was removed. This is a hard break for R4 messages that used it to distinguish a final target device from an intermediary destination endpoint. The apparent alternatives in R6 require interpretation and may not preserve the old routing semantics.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Any R4 instance carrying `destination.target` is invalid against the R6 base resource. R6 has no same-named field, so strict parsers will reject or drop the old data. The issue is primarily R4→R6; reverse conversion is not applicable because R6 no longer has this element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory messages using `destination.target`. If the target Device corresponds to a known network endpoint, create/reference an Endpoint and populate `destination.endpointReference`; otherwise consider `destination.receiver` only when it truly represents the intended real-world recipient. Use extensions or manual review when the old target was strictly a routing-hop identifier.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal may be intended to consolidate routing around Endpoint and receiver references, but without an explicit replacement it is not clearly backward-compatible. Keeping a deprecated optional target would have preserved legacy multi-hop routing while allowing profiles to discourage new use.

findings.title: MessageHeader.enterer was removed

oldState.summary: Optional Reference to Practitioner or PractitionerRole identifying the data entry performer.

semanticText.short: The source of the data entry
semanticText.definition: The person or device that performed the data entry leading to this message. When there is more than one candidate, pick the most proximal to the message. Can provide other enterers in extensions.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 carried a local data-entry participant on the MessageHeader itself.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removed this local audit/provenance participant element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `enterer` are invalid in R6 and the information has no same-path replacement. The element was optional, so prevalence depends on audit practices, but systems that used it for traceability or authorization need a separate provenance strategy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Data-entry attribution can matter for audit, authorization, and incident review.

justification.inferredGoal: Move participant attribution out of MessageHeader and into workflow/provenance resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain optional `enterer` as deprecated and recommend Provenance or Task for richer attribution.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving data-entry attribution toward Provenance, Task, or event-specific workflow resources is reasonable. The supplied artifacts do not show that R6 needed to reject existing `enterer` data in the base resource, and the element was optional, so a deprecated compatibility field could have supported gradual migration. The removal was therefore probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design would leave `MessageHeader.enterer` as an optional legacy element and document a preferred `Provenance.agent` or Task mapping for new R6 implementations. This preserves R4 validation and audit traceability while implementations migrate. The main cost is overlapping attribution locations and the possibility that the deprecated field remains in use.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Allows duplicated attribution between MessageHeader and workflow/provenance resources, requiring reconciliation rules, but preserves old audit data.

evidence.detail: R4 has enterer as 0..1 Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole).
evidence.quote: The person or device that performed the data entry leading to this message.

evidence.detail: R6 MessageHeader has no element id `MessageHeader.enterer`.

examples.examplesMd: The Provenance fragment is illustrative; exact agent type coding and target references need local policy.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageHeader.enterer` was removed. Existing R4 messages can carry data-entry attribution directly; R6 MessageHeader cannot, so migrations must preserve the attribution elsewhere if it is operationally or legally relevant.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is an old-valid/new-invalid element removal. Strict R6 validation rejects the `enterer` property. There is no R6-to-R4 representability issue from this change because R6 no longer defines the element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `enterer` to Provenance, AuditEvent, Task, or an extension according to local governance. Test downstream audit and authorization workflows that previously read `MessageHeader.enterer`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removing an optional attribution element is disruptive when used. A deprecation period or standard cross-version extension would have allowed old messages to validate while encouraging richer Provenance usage.

findings.title: MessageHeader.author was removed

oldState.summary: Optional Reference to Practitioner or PractitionerRole identifying the logical author/source of decision.

semanticText.definition: The logical author of the message - the person or device that decided the described event should happen. When there is more than one candidate, pick the most proximal to the MessageHeader. Can provide other authors in extensions.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented the decision author directly on MessageHeader.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removed this local author/decision participant element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances carrying `author` are invalid in R6 and the author role must be represented outside MessageHeader. The break is optional-element-dependent but important for workflows that distinguish data entry from clinical or operational decision authority.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Author attribution can affect accountability, audit, and clinical/business responsibility.

justification.inferredGoal: Shift message participant attribution to workflow/provenance resources rather than the header.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain optional `author` as deprecated and publish a preferred Provenance or Task mapping.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: It is reasonable for R6 to encourage authorship and decision attribution outside MessageHeader. Still, the R4 `author` element carried a distinct role, was optional, and could have remained valid while newer resources became the preferred representation. Without an exact local replacement, the hard removal was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The compatible base design is to keep `MessageHeader.author` as an optional deprecated element and define a recommended mapping to `Provenance.agent`, Task requester/owner, or event-specific resources. This would preserve R4 messages and let profiles tighten future use. The tradeoff is a longer period with duplicate authorship representations and possible inconsistencies.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy authorship but can duplicate or conflict with richer workflow/provenance attribution unless precedence is profiled.

evidence.detail: R4 has author as 0..1 Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole).
evidence.quote: The logical author of the message - the person or device that decided the described event should happen.

evidence.detail: R6 MessageHeader has no element id `MessageHeader.author`.

examples.examplesMd: The replacement is not computably specified by MessageHeader; use profile-specific Provenance or Task rules.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageHeader.author` was removed. This is not just a code cleanup: it removes a local place to state who decided the event should happen, which can be distinct from the data-enterer, sender, or responsible organization.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 messages with `author` fail R6 base validation. No R6 same-path field exists, so old parsers and code generators cannot preserve this value without an explicit extension or separate resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map author attribution to Provenance.agent, Task requester/owner, or an implementation-specific extension after confirming the intended role. Regression-test workflows that used MessageHeader author for authorization or audit display.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated optional field or cross-version extension would have been less disruptive. The likely benefit of removal is simpler MessageHeader participant modeling, but that benefit depends on consistent use of other resources.

findings.title: MessageHeader.responsible was removed

oldState.summary: Optional Reference to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization accepting overall responsibility.

semanticText.definition: The person or organization that accepts overall responsibility for the contents of the message. The implication is that the message event happened under the policies of the responsible party.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed the header to name the party accepting overall responsibility for the message contents.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removed this local responsibility/attestation participant element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 messages using `responsible` become invalid in R6. The removed content can be business-critical because it identifies the policy-responsible party, not merely a technical sender.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Responsibility attribution can have compliance, authorization, and accountability consequences.

justification.inferredGoal: Move responsibility attribution out of MessageHeader into workflow, Task, Provenance, or other event-specific resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain optional `responsible` as deprecated and define a standard mapping to Provenance, Task, or event-specific responsibility.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Shifting responsibility attribution into workflow or provenance resources is a reasonable modeling direction, but `responsible` captures accountability that is not necessarily equivalent to sender, receiver, author, or endpoint. Because the R6 artifacts do not provide an exact replacement, retaining the optional element during transition would have preserved old instances with manageable tradeoffs. The removal was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep `MessageHeader.responsible` as `0..1 Reference` with deprecated/legacy guidance and publish mappings to Provenance, Task, or the focus resource where appropriate. That preserves old accountability data while steering new implementations away from header-level responsibility. The cost is continued overlap and the need for rules when both legacy and richer responsibility data are present.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps overlapping accountability representations but avoids rejecting potentially compliance-relevant responsibility data.

evidence.detail: R4 has responsible as 0..1 Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole|Organization).
evidence.quote: The person or organization that accepts overall responsibility for the contents of the message.

evidence.detail: R6 MessageHeader has no element id `MessageHeader.responsible`.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates preserving responsibility outside MessageHeader; the exact Provenance role coding should be profiled.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageHeader.responsible` was removed. This creates a hard validation break and a semantic migration problem for systems that record who accepts responsibility for message content.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `responsible` are invalid in R6. The loss is semantic as well as structural because no R6 MessageHeader field has the same responsibility meaning.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not blindly map `responsible` to sender or receiver. Determine whether the value represents a legal organization, accountable clinician, or workflow owner, then map to Provenance, Task, event-specific focus resources, or an extension. Include human review for records where accountability is legally relevant.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal may simplify MessageHeader, but without a formal replacement it was probably avoidable from a backward-compatibility perspective. A deprecated optional element would have preserved old responsibility data during migration.

findings.title: MessageHeader.event[x] added canonical EventDefinition/SubscriptionTopic choice

oldState.summary: Required choice of Coding or uri; example binding to message-events.

binding.description: One of the message events defined as part of this version of FHIR.

semanticText.short: Code for the event this message represents or link to event definition

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 event could be a Coding or URI, serialized as `eventCoding` or `eventUri`.

newState.summary: Required choice of Coding, uri, or canonical targeting EventDefinition or SubscriptionTopic.

binding.description: One of the message events defined as part of this version of FHIR.

semanticText.short: The real world event that triggered this messsage
semanticText.definition: Events are defined by codes, or by URIs that identify events, or by reference to EventDefinition or SubscriptionTopic resources that define the event directly.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds `eventCanonical` and text saying event selection is intentionally delegated to implementations and implementation guides.

facts.note: R6 explicitly states that event selection is delegated to implementations and implementation guides.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 Coding and URI event values remain valid choices in R6, so this is not an old-valid/new-invalid change. The risk is reverse conversion and runtime compatibility: R6 instances can use `eventCanonical`, a JSON choice arm absent in R4, and dispatch code that switches only on Coding/uri may miss R6 canonical events.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Event identity drives message behavior; failing to interpret a canonical event can trigger the wrong workflow or no workflow.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow messages to point directly at formal EventDefinition or SubscriptionTopic resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `eventCanonical` preserves R4 Coding and uri instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding a canonical choice for EventDefinition or SubscriptionTopic is a reasonable way to make message events more computable. Since R4 `eventCoding` and `eventUri` values remain valid in R6, this finding is not an old-valid/new-invalid base-design break. The residual compatibility issue is reverse conversion and runtime handling of a new R6 choice arm.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is needed to preserve R4-to-R6 validity because the change is additive. A URI-only design would make R6-to-R4 projection easier, but it would lose the stronger canonical target-profile semantics that the R6 choice provides.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is R6-to-R4 conversion loss and codegen updates, not a less-breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.

evidence.detail: R4 event[x] types are Coding and uri.
R6 event[x] adds canonical target profiles EventDefinition and SubscriptionTopic.
R6 definition says event codes/URIs/canonical definitions are implementation- or IG-selected.
evidence.quote: This element is intentionally unbound, and the selection of appropriate event codes is delegated to implementations and implementation guides.

examples.examplesMd: Projecting an R6 canonical to R4 `eventUri` is syntactically plausible but loses the explicit canonical choice type and target-profile semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: `event[x]` was widened with a canonical choice. This is not a hard R4→R6 validation break, but it is material for cross-version converters and generated models because R6 introduces a new event arm and emphasizes implementation-defined event catalogs.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old `eventCoding` and `eventUri` values remain valid in R6. An R6 `eventCanonical` value is not a legal R4 property; a converter must downgrade it to `eventUri`, use an extension, or reject it. Runtime dispatch code must handle the new canonical branch.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 models and dispatch logic to accept `eventCanonical`. For R6→R4, decide whether canonical URLs can be safely serialized as `eventUri` and document the loss of target-profile typing. Include tests for all three event choice arms.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is mostly additive and justified, but official conversion guidance would reduce ambiguity. Keeping only URI would have preserved R4 shape but weakened R6 semantic typing.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The binding metadata remains `example`; the material mechanical change is the added canonical choice, not a binding-strength change.

findings.title: MessageHeader.destination.receiver now allows Device, Patient, and RelatedPerson references

oldState.summary: Optional receiver Reference to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 limited destination receiver to practitioner, practitioner role, or organization recipients.

newState.summary: Optional receiver Reference also allows Device, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 widens destination receiver to include device, patient, and related person recipients.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a permissive R6 widening, so existing R4 receiver references remain valid. R6 messages can now name receivers that R4 validators reject. Generated code that restricts receiver targets to the R4 set may also reject valid R6 content.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Recipient identity affects routing and access-control decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent real-world recipients beyond organizations and practitioners.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 widens receiver target profiles while retaining all R4 target profiles.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing Device, Patient, and RelatedPerson receivers is a reasonable base R6 expressivity improvement, and it does not invalidate any R4 `destination.receiver` instance because all prior target profiles are retained. The breakage is limited to reverse conversion or R4-era generated validators that cannot accept the widened R6 domain.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4-to-R6 preservation. Keeping the new receiver types only in profiles or extensions would improve R6-to-R4 projection, but it would reduce base interoperability for recipient types that R6 deliberately made first-class.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 converters must handle new target types, but old R4 receiver references are preserved.

evidence.detail: R4 receiver target profiles are Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Organization.
R6 receiver target profiles add Device, Patient, and RelatedPerson.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is valid only for the widened R6 target set; R4 needs an extension, alternate routing field, or a different recipient representation.

findings.narrativeMd: `destination.receiver` broadened its reference target domain. This is not a forward validation break, but it is important for reverse conversion and generated validators.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: All R4 receiver targets are still accepted in R6. R6 Device, Patient, or RelatedPerson receiver references are not valid in R4 for this element, so R6→R4 conversion needs a policy or loses receiver specificity.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 validators and generated models to allow the new target types. For R6→R4, reject unsupported receiver targets, map them through extensions, or use profile-specific routing conventions. Test access-control and routing code with each new target type.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The widening is likely justified by real-world routing needs. A less disruptive approach would keep the base list narrow and allow new targets by profile, but that fragments interoperability.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, type, kind, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. Status changed from draft to active and is reported as non-breaking notable.
No local min increased or max narrowed. The material endpoint min decreases from 1 to 0 are captured in endpoint findings because they affect R6→R4 representability.

All material local type-domain changes found are represented in findings. `MessageHeader.response.details`, `focus`, `definition`, `reason`, names, source software/version/contact, destination name, and response code retain their core types.

`response.code` remains required against `ValueSet/response-code`, and the local CodeSystem concepts `ok`, `transient-error`, and `fatal-error` are unchanged. `event[x]` and `reason` retain example-strength bindings. Full terminology expansions were not available.

No local MessageHeader-specific invariant additions, removals, or strengthenings were identified. Snapshot changes to inherited `ele-1`/`ext-1` constraints and xpath fields are out of scope for this artifact.
No local MessageHeader element changed modifier status. Base modifierExtension-related changes are inherited and out of scope.
Local MessageHeader business elements retained summary=true where relevant. Inherited DomainResource `modifierExtension` summary flag changes are excluded.
No local fixed, pattern, or default values were identified on MessageHeader elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex restrictions changed for MessageHeader elements.
No local slicing changes were identified in the MessageHeader snapshots/differentials.
Material serialization changes are captured in findings for response.identifier and endpoint choice conversions. No additional local serialization-only changes were identified.

Known R6-to-R4 risks are captured for Identifier, Endpoint references/omitted endpoints, canonical event values, sender target widening, and receiver target widening. Exact lossless conversion depends on local resources and policies.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact status changed from draft to active while identity stayed stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Status metadata does not change instance JSON validity or the resource canonical identity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers may treat R6 MessageHeader as more mature, but should not infer that local element migration is trivial.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: focus definition now explicitly says Parameters is allowed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `focus` remains `Reference(Resource)` with the same cardinality, so the computable type already accommodates resource references; the text clarification does not invalidate R4 content.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 implementations should be prepared for focus references to Parameters in message workflows.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: response.code ValueSet version changed but required codes appear unchanged
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The required binding still includes CodeSystem `http://hl7.org/fhir/response-code`, and the local R4/R6 CodeSystems both define `ok`, `transient-error`, and `fatal-error` with matching meanings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated enum names should still be checked against the R6 package version, but no code removal was found.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Example-strength event and reason bindings retain their primary ValueSet URLs
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both bindings are example strength, so changes in their illustrative value sets do not directly invalidate instances. The material event change is the added canonical choice, reported separately.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementation guides should still review their own event and reason code systems because R6 text emphasizes implementation-selected events.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited changes such as Resource.language binding, modifierExtension summary flags, base constraints, and extension constraint snapshots are materially relevant to validation but are excluded from this local MessageHeader report.
R6 endpoint[x] can reference Endpoint resources; lossless R6→R4 conversion depends on whether an Endpoint can be resolved to an R4 URL endpoint.
R6 eventCanonical targets these resources; conversion and dispatch behavior depend on how event definitions/topics are represented and versioned.
Removed participant elements (`enterer`, `author`, `responsible`) and the R6 comment on sender likely require mapping to Provenance or Task in real implementations.
Search parameters were out of scope, but path changes such as `sender` to `source.sender` and endpoint choice conversion may affect search behavior and client queries.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 diff, Jira rationale, or committee change note was used. Structural conclusions are high-confidence, but intent and best replacement semantics for removed fields are less certain.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official change proposals, ballot reconciliation notes, or an HL7-published diff for MessageHeader.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official cross-version ConceptMap/StructureMap was found for MessageHeader. Migration guidance for removed fields and semantic identity changes is therefore based on StructureDefinition evidence and FHIR modeling judgement.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use an official R4↔R6 conversion map if one becomes available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Full terminology expansions were not available in the local packages for the checked ValueSets. Response-code was cross-checked via local CodeSystems, but expansion-based equivalence was not performed.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run a terminology server expansion for the R4 and R6 ValueSets and compare system/code/display/definition changes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Endpoint, EventDefinition, SubscriptionTopic, Provenance, Task, and related workflow resources were not analyzed in depth. That limits confidence in lossless replacement recommendations, not in the existence of the MessageHeader deltas.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the assigned reports for those resources/datatypes and any official workflow guidance.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative specification pages beyond generated StructureDefinition text were not reviewed. This especially matters for the R6 source.sender comment that proposes possible future removal in favor of Task.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the R6 ballot MessageHeader narrative page and related issue history.
